economy.summary: Her campaign platform supports raising Pennsylvania's minimum wage, noting it has remained $7.25 for nearly two decades, and proposes education, union support, and training centers to prepare workers for emerging industries such as AI, robotics, and advanced batteries.
economy.short: Supports raising minimum wage; proposes worker training for emerging industries.

education.summary: Her campaign platform supports Pennsylvania's adequacy funding formula that sends the most help to the schools that need it most, citing disparities where some districts offer career and technical programs while others borrow money to keep classrooms open.
education.short: Supports adequacy funding formula directing most help to neediest schools.

healthcare.summary: Her campaign platform says healthcare access in Washington County should not depend on location or employment, cites Medicaid cuts affecting more than 300,000 Pennsylvanians as a concern, and calls for raising healthcare provider reimbursement rates that have not kept pace with costs.
healthcare.short: Says access shouldn't depend on location; cites Medicaid cut concerns.

energy.summary: Her campaign platform proposes pursuing renewable energy, electrification, and battery manufacturing alongside the region's traditional energy sectors, arguing that unstable global markets and climate change make economic diversification necessary.
energy.short: Proposes renewables and battery manufacturing alongside traditional energy sectors.

economy.summary: Says the only way to raise state revenue without digging deeper into Pennsylvanians' pockets is to grow the economy, proposing to remove government barriers that make it harder to save money, get to work, and earn, and backing permitting changes to allow a liquefied natural gas facility in Philadelphia.
economy.short: Proposes growing economy and removing barriers instead of raising taxes.

taxes.summary: Voted for the $50.8 billion 2026-27 state budget, saying it reduced the governor's proposed spending, avoided tapping the Rainy Day Fund, and imposes no new taxes; he had earlier opposed Gov. Shapiro's budget proposal, saying the state cannot continue to rely on new taxes and accounting tricks to fill gaps.
taxes.short: Supported 2026-27 budget with no new taxes, reduced spending.

abortion.summary: As a legislator, he cosponsored a proposed constitutional amendment stating the Pennsylvania Constitution does not grant a right to abortion (HB 2252, 2022), voted for SB 106 (2022), a package containing that amendment, and voted for bills prohibiting abortions sought because of a Down syndrome diagnosis (HB 1500, 2021; HB 321, 2019).
abortion.short: Cosponsored no-right-to-abortion amendment; voted for Down syndrome abortion bans.

education.summary: His campaign platform argues Pennsylvania spends adequately per pupil but that schools face excessive unfunded state mandates, supports local school board autonomy, and identifies $70 billion in unfunded public pension debt as a major crisis for school funding.
education.short: Says per-pupil spending adequate; opposes unfunded mandates; cites pension debt.

healthcare.summary: His campaign platform addresses healthcare through the opioid epidemic, which he says should be treated as a public health crisis, advocating increased funding for addiction treatment and restoring a cabinet-level Department of Drug and Alcohol Programs; the platform does not detail a broader healthcare position.
healthcare.short: Advocates treating opioid epidemic as public health crisis; funding treatment.

energy.summary: Voted for a 2025-26 budget package that he says removes Pennsylvania from the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative, which he describes as a multi-state carbon tax compact that has driven up energy prices, and supports permitting reform to revitalize the state's energy industry and bring down energy costs.
energy.short: Supports leaving RGGI and permitting reform to lower energy costs.

guns.summary: On public safety, he announced a resolution to impeach an Allegheny County magisterial district judge over no-cash bail releases, saying a judge who lets dangerous suspects on the street as a matter of routine policy poses a danger to all Pennsylvanians; this is a bail and courts position rather than a firearms position.
guns.short: Announced impeachment resolution against judge over no-cash bail releases.
